summary: A two-day Maharashtrian wedding for 200 guests in Mumbai on a ₹10,00,000 budget: Day 1 brings Halad Chadavne (haldi), mehendi and a family Sangeet, and Day 2 is the Simant Pujan, Antarpat, Mangalashtak and Saptapadi followed by a short evening reception. Catering and the venue take over half the budget, so we assumed a banquet hall in Dadar, Thane or Navi Mumbai rather than a hotel ballroom, a pure-vegetarian traditional menu, and that most guests live in or near Mumbai. With about four months to go, venue, caterer and photographer should be locked in this month because good Muhurat dates book out fast.

budget.tips: Book a banquet hall for two days on a weekday-evening or package rate and ask for the basic stage and lighting to be included. Reuse the Day 2 mandap flowers for the reception backdrop.

Choose a traditional Maharashtrian thali (puran poli, masale bhaat, varan-bhaat, shrikhand) at ₹900 to ₹1,100 per plate instead of a multi-cuisine buffet, and confirm a final headcount two weeks out to avoid paying for extra plates.
Hire one lead photographer plus one candid shooter for Day 2 and a single photographer for the Day 1 functions. Skip the drone and the printed album, and take a digital gallery instead.
Buy the bride's Paithani or Nauvari saree and rent the groom's pheta and sherwani set. Rent statement jewellery such as the nath and tanmani for the ceremony and use family heirlooms for the rest.
Ask the priest for one consolidated samagri list and buy it in bulk from a Dadar market wholesaler. Book a single sanai and dhol-tasha group for both the varat and the ceremony.
Keep the Sangeet a family-performance evening with a DJ for two hours rather than a hired choreographer, and use fresh marigold and turmeric from the market for the haldi set-up.
Block rooms only for out-of-town elders at a budget hotel near the venue, and arrange a single hired tempo traveller for the varat and airport or station pick-ups.
Send a WhatsApp e-invite to most guests and print cards only for elders and close relatives. Choose a useful return gift such as a potted tulsi or a steel dabba.
Hold this reserve back until the final week. It typically absorbs last-minute headcount increases, extra decor flowers and vendor overtime.

Book a banquet hall in Dadar, Thane or Navi Mumbai for both days and pay the booking advance
Book the caterer after a trial of puran poli, masale bhaat and shrikhand, and lock the per-plate rate in writing
Book the photographer and videographer for Day 1 and Day 2
Shop for the bride's Paithani or Nauvari saree, Shalu, and the groom's pheta and kurta, and order tailoring
Book the mehendi artist and the bridal makeup artist for the two days
Design the invitation (digital plus a small print run) and finalise wording for both days
Send invitations and open RSVPs on WhatsApp, with printed cards for elders
Reserve a block of rooms and a tempo traveller for out-of-town guests
Finalise the mandap, Antarpat cloth and floral decor theme with the decorator
Book the sanai and dhol-tasha group for the varat, and a DJ with sound for the Sangeet
Collect the full pooja samagri list from the priest and order the items
Order return gifts and welcome hampers for out-of-town guests
Complete outfit and jewellery fittings and fix any alterations
Confirm the final headcount with the caterer and the venue
Prepare documents for marriage registration: ID and address proofs, photographs and the invitation card
Walk through the venue with the decorator, caterer and photographer and share a written run-of-show
Host the Kelvan, the pre-wedding feast, for close relatives at home
Give each family helper a named responsibility and pack ceremonial items, the Mundavalya and the Mangalsutra

Day 2: Simant Pujan, Gaurihar Pooja, Antarpat, Mangalashtak, Kanyadaan and Saptapadi

Confirm the dressing room and green room for the bride and groom

Agree the per-plate price and the number of meals across both days
Confirm a live counter for jalebi or chaat and the service staff count
Ask about a Jain and no-onion-no-garlic option for a few guests
Settle the final headcount deadline and the extra-plate rate
Review recent Maharashtrian wedding albums from the photographer
Confirm hours of coverage for both days and the number of team members
Agree on the delivery timeline for the digital gallery and highlight reel
Share a must-capture list: Antarpat, Saptapadi, Kanyadaan and family portraits
Fix the Muhurat and the schedule for each ritual with the priest
Get the pooja samagri list and the dakshina agreed in advance
Book the sanai and dhol-tasha group for the varat and the entrance
Confirm who will arrange the Mundavalya, Mangalsutra and Akshata
Place tailoring orders early for the Paithani or Nauvari saree blouse and groom's outfit
Confirm jewellery on rent or purchase, including the nath and tanmani
Book the bridal makeup trial two weeks before the wedding
Plan matching outfits for close family on Day 1 and Day 2
Book the mehendi artist for the bride and a few family members
Arrange turmeric, marigold and mango leaves for the haldi
Book a DJ, sound and a small stage for the Sangeet
Agree on a list of family performances and rehearsal slots

ideas.title: Paithani-inspired mandap
ideas.description: Drape the stage in peacock and lotus Paithani motifs in maroon, gold and green, with marigold and mogra garlands. It photographs beautifully and reads as unmistakably Maharashtrian.

ideas.title: Dhol-tasha varat entrance
ideas.description: Welcome the groom's procession with a dhol-tasha troupe and a sanai player, then switch to soft sanai for the Antarpat moment so the energy builds toward the ceremony.

ideas.title: Eco-friendly haldi
ideas.description: Use fresh turmeric paste, marigold petals and a mango-leaf toran instead of synthetic colour, and let guests apply it with small brass bowls that double as return gifts.

ideas.title: Tulsi sapling return gifts
ideas.description: Gift each family a small tulsi sapling in a clay pot with a handwritten thank-you tag. It is affordable, sustainable and ties back to the Griha Pravesh tradition.

ideas.title: Street-food reception counter
ideas.description: Add a small live counter of vada pav, misal and cutting chai at the evening reception, a nostalgic Mumbai touch that is cheaper than an extra buffet station.

ideas.title: Sangeet family story reel
ideas.description: Ask each side for three childhood photos and play a short slideshow between performances. It makes the Sangeet personal without paying for a choreographer.
